note: The living city's rules as data: one file read by the viewer (docs/city/core.mjs) and the Python core (smc.city.rules). Amounts are in whole currency units (Credits, a placeholder currency at par with the US dollar so real-world figures read as they are). Every figure says where it comes from; 'approx.' marks a figure taken as representative where the exact schedule varies by place or could not be confirmed.

clock.basis: a game day is 72 real minutes: 48 from sunrise to sunset, 24 from sunset to the next sunrise (2026-11-14: real darkness was unplayable). The sun keeps its real path for the game date at San Francisco; day k starts at sunrise of start + k days, at real epoch + k cycles. The books (hours, shifts, pay, rent, NPC days, the sky) read the game clock; what moves moves in real seconds (clock.mjs)

jurisdictions.basis: approx. city limits as boxes [west, south, east, north]; the county where no city box holds the point

income.basis: single filer. Federal: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (tax year 2026). California: FTB 2025 schedule (the latest published; indexed each year) and the 1% Behavioral Health Services tax over 1,000,000.

payroll.basis: employee shares, 2026: Social Security 6.2% to the wage base (SSA), Medicare 1.45% and 0.9% more over 200,000 (IRS), California SDI on all wages (EDD; approx. 1.3% for 2026)

sales.basis: combined state, county and district rates (CDTFA); approx. where a city's district taxes changed during the year

property.basis: Proposition 13: 1% of assessed value, plus each area's voter-approved debt and parcel levies; the assessed value is the price paid, raised at most 2% a year. Totals approx. (secured roll 2025-26).

transfer.basis: paid by the seller when real estate changes hands. Every county: the documentary transfer tax, 1.10 per 1,000. Cities add their own: San Francisco's whole-value tiers (Business and Tax Regulations Code art. 12-C, as of 2024); Oakland's tiers (Measure X); approx. elsewhere.

vehicle.basis: California: vehicle license fee 0.65% of value a year (DMV), registration and CHP fees, and the transportation improvement fee by value (approx. 2026)

fuel.basis: per US gallon: California excise 61.2c (July 2025 - June 2026), federal excise 18.4c, sales tax on the rest; price before taxes approx.

local.basis: San Francisco: parking tax 25% of off-street parking (Business and Tax Regulations Code art. 9); hotel tax 14%

tolls.basis: Bay Area Toll Authority's seven bridges: 8.50 for a two-axle car from 1 January 2026 (BATA 2026 toll increase), taken one way only; carpools of three or more with a FasTrak CAV tag pay half on weekdays 5-10 and 15-19 (approx.). Golden Gate Bridge: southbound only, set by its district (approx. FasTrak 9.75, invoice 10.75). Without FasTrak an invoice is mailed, due in 21 days; unpaid, a violation notice adds a penalty, then a second.

managed_lanes.basis: lanes from OpenStreetMap (hov:lanes, hov:minimum, hov:conditional, toll:hov; scripts/build_managed_lanes.py). Carpool lanes: two or more (or as signed) in the hours posted. Express lanes (Bay Area Express Lanes, VTA, 101 Express): solo drivers pay a price set by congestion, shown at the entrance; carpools free or half with a FasTrak Flex set to their size. Driving solo in a carpool lane is a violation of at least 490 with penalty assessments (California Vehicle Code 21655.5).

enforcement.basis: San Francisco's automated speed cameras (2025 pilot): 50 for 11-15 mph over, 100 for 16-25, 200 for 26 and over, 500 at 100 mph or faster; parking citations approx. SFMTA schedule

witness.basis: a moving violation (speeding, a carpool lane short of its riders) is charged only where it is seen: in the field of view of one of the map's enforcement cameras (the speed cameras drawn on their poles; each looks along its street, a 70-degree cone out to 45 m, approx. a fixed camera's working range), or with a patrol car within 60 m

vehicles.basis: new prices approx. 2026 California list (the vision's new economy car: 22,000); used by age so a five-year-old hatchback is the vision's 8,000; fuel use EPA combined

water.basis: salinity in practical salinity units (about grams of salt a kilogram); density from UNESCO's equation of state at 15 C, simplified: 999.1 + 0.77 x salinity kg/m3. Corrosion relative to fresh water, after typical carbon-steel loss rates. Bay zones approx. after USGS San Francisco Bay salinity surveys.

zones.basis: San Pablo Bay (approx. 20 in the dry season, much fresher after rain)
the South Bay's former salt ponds, from the map's outlines where named
South Bay below the San Mateo Bridge (approx. 26)

jobs.basis: occupations by workplace; pay an hour on the V2 vision's scale: a basic job pays 120 every 10 minutes of active work (720 an hour, the floor), and every other role keeps its ratio to San Francisco's minimum wage (19.18 from 1 July 2025) in the BLS OEWS 2024 hourly medians for San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont. Shifts as such places keep them.

density.basis: how busy the streets are beyond the residents' own days: passers-by to a 150 m square of streets at the busiest hour, and a multiplier on them and on through traffic -- by default, and in the hotspots (the busiest wins). The Marina is the test district: Chestnut and Union Streets, the Marina Green and the Palace of Fine Arts. Nobody is made up where you look (docs/city/fleet.mjs): the residents are each home's, and the through traffic is a fleet of visitors' cars -- so many to a place of the district by how busy it is, each coming through 4 to 9 times a day from the edge of the streets (a through trip, or about half the time a stop: parked near a shop and an hour or so on foot about the shops) -- sized so the Marina's streets carry the traffic of a busy neighbourhood street (approx.: a busy neighbourhood shopping street carries several thousand to fifteen thousand vehicles a day).
density.walks_basis: the game's day is 72 minutes and a walk takes as long as it really does, so a day's walking done in it is some twenty times what is out on the pavements at once: only this share of the residents' walks is seen (the rest are out of sight, as most of the through traffic is: through_driven), and none that would have someone out more than walk_early_max game minutes before the thing they are going to (leaving at 3 a.m. for an 8 o'clock start). Calibrated on the real Marina (tests/city_density.test.mjs) so that the busiest block at its busiest hour has about forty people out and a busy street eight to ten a block (the user's count, 2026-11-20).

trim.basis: the redundant are not made: a flatmate, or a partner in a home with no children, in one of the big trades whose members share one story and voice (npc-stories.mjs), with no part the district needs (no counter, round, vehicle or school)

commuters.basis: people who live outside the district and work outside it, seen only as they drive through, once a game day, on the through routes; sized so the rush hours carry about what Lombard and Marina Boulevard do (Caltrans: approx. 50,000 a day on Lombard) seen at real speed in the 72-minute day

traffic.basis: where and when the through traffic goes. Drivers keep to the main streets: a way's cost is its time at the limit times its class's preference, cheaper still on a named corridor (by its weight). Through trips start and end at the edge of the streets, a gate on a corridor that much likelier than a side street's, and a share of them run the length of one corridor end to end. Lombard Street is US 101 through the Marina (Caltrans counts approx. 50,000 vehicles a day between Richardson Avenue and Van Ness, about twelve times a typical residential street's); Marina Boulevard, Divisadero, Fillmore, Chestnut and Bay carry approx. 8,000 to 20,000. By the hour: two rush hours (7-9 and 4-7) at the full count, the middle of the day at about 60%, the night at under a fifth; commuters keep to the rush hours, deliveries to the working day, ride-hail to the evening too. At a signal on a main street the main street has the longer green (approx. 60% of the cycle), as SFMTA times Lombard's.

maneuvers.basis: what a turn costs a driver choosing a way, in seconds (after Valhalla's auto costing: a turn with the traffic is cheap, a turn across it dear, back the way it came dearest), so routes keep to right turns where they can

routine.basis: a 24-hour day around each person's shift: sleep, getting ready, the commute, a break mid-shift, errands and meals out, an evening out for some, home and sleep

repair.basis: what breaks (a window, a door, a shopfront) stays broken for half a day, is boarded over with plywood planks, and is back as it was within three days (approx. a glazier's or carpenter's turnaround for a city repair); not yet triggered by anything that breaks

vitals.basis: three bars from 0 to 100. Stamina runs down through the waking day and with effort (sprinting, a shift at work, a workout) and comes back at night, faster asleep at home or in a hotel; food and drink give it back. Health wears down slowly, quickly with no stamina left, and comes back with medicine, a doctor's visit and nights asleep; at none you faint, wake at home and are billed for the ambulance. Strength fades a little each day; workouts at a gym build it, and walking a little. Strength sets how much you can carry. Time away is lived as days are: awake by day, asleep at home by night.

items.basis: what the city's shops sell, on the V2 vision's price scale (a simple meal 35, clothing 100-500). kind is the sales-tax class (groceries and prescriptions are exempt in California). kg is what it weighs to carry; a service is used where it is bought. use is what it does to the bars when used.

stores.basis: what each kind of store sells, by the kinds the map's tenants are (OpenStreetMap shop and amenity tags, and for clinics and gyms the tenant's name). A building with several tenants has a store for each.
stores.tenants_basis: the tenant's name tells what kind of place it is where the map's tag is too coarse (shop) or wrong (a dentist tagged a pharmacy, an architect's office tagged a shop): each rule's kind takes the place of the tags it replaces, and within a group only the first matching rule counts, and the first rule that applies decides alone unless it is one that combines (a deli and a liquor store are often one shop). A null kind is no shop at all (an office, a church, a school).

tenants.pattern: ice cream|gelato|creamery|frozen yogh?urt|ben & jerry|baskin|swensen|smitten|salt & straw|bi-rite creamery
burger|\bwings?\b|chicken|smokehouse|steak|tavern|\bpub\b|bbq|barbecue|five guys|shake shack|in-n-out|super duper|wendy|mcdonald|carl'?s jr|jack in the box|popeyes|kfc

fixtures.basis: what a shopper uses in a store and leaves there: never on a shelf, never sold (docs/53-store-catalogue.md). container: what it holds, as rules items container. Drawn from docs/city/objects.json items (the carts) and fixtures (the checkout).

handling.basis: how things are picked up, held, thrown and swung, and how high you jump. Lifting: one object up to 12 kg + 0.6 kg a point of strength (24 kg at 20, 72 kg at 100; untrained adults lift about a third of their weight from the floor, trained ones their own weight). Throwing: the arm gives 40-220 J by strength (an untrained throw of a 0.15 kg ball is about 25 m/s, 45 J), capped at 14-30 m/s for light things; under 3 m/s it is no throw. Swinging: rigid things up to 30% of what you can lift, the blow's energy by mass and length. Jumping: the legs push over 42% of their length (53% of height) with 1.6-3.0 body weights by strength (untrained to athletic: 0.3 to 0.8 m), against body and load (approx., after published sports-science figures). material_of, hold and length_m on each item say what it is made of, how it is held (hand, two_hands, shoulder, tool) and how long it is.

found.basis: nothing is left lying on the pavement for anyone to find: what is picked up in the street is a task's (a courier's order at its shop's door) or what someone put down. A crash leaves debris to see, never parts to take (commerce.outcomes). per_district 0 turns the seeded finds off; items are what they were, for a district that turns them back on

transit.basis: the V2 vision's bus trip (15, paid boarding); taxis metered from the flag drop, by the kilometre (approx.)

delivery.basis: a delivery gig: a parcel from a restaurant, café or shop to a home 200 to 900 m away, paid when handed over, half pay if late; gig pay is not withheld from

business.basis: the V2 vision's leases (a storefront 3,000 a week); the rest is docs/37-business-legal-and-careers-plan.md, built in docs/city/enterprise.mjs. Money here is only ever under the money keys (fee_base, price, pay, balance); shares, weights and counts never are.
business.licences_basis: approx. San Francisco's schedule: the Business Registration Certificate (Treasurer and Tax Collector, smallest tier), a Department of Public Health retail food permit (approx. 380-1,100 by size), a California ABC on-sale licence (approx. 1,200 new)
business.wholesale_basis: what a shop pays its wholesaler, as a share of the list price, approx. by kind (food service 30-45% food cost, grocery 70-75% of shelf, general retail about half)
business.elasticity_basis: demand falls with price: groceries elastic (approx. -1.2), prepared food less so (approx. -0.6)
business.customers_basis: a shop's walk-ins an hour at its busiest (approx., by kind: a cafe 40, a restaurant 30, a corner shop 25, a boutique 8), shaped by the hour, shared with the rivals of its kind within 600 m, raised by its name and lowered by its prices
business.staff_basis: people ask at least the minimum wage and about their role's going rate for their skill; morale falls with understaffed shifts and pay below the going rate, and rises with raises and breaks (late below 30, a week's notice below 15)
business.wage_scale_basis: a shop's economy is the real one, as its prices are (a coffee 8): the wages it pays are real San Francisco wages, the jobs' pay (the V2 vision's scale, 720 an hour the floor) times 19.18 / 720 -- the minimum wage 19.18 an hour, a barista about 21
business.buying_basis: a small business sells for about 2.5 times its trailing year's profit plus its stock at cost; a shop that makes nothing is asked its stock and a key fee; seller financing as such sales are usually done (30% down, the rest over two years at about 8%)
business.law_basis: invented lawyers at the map's real law offices (the office's name is the building's, its people are not real); fees approx. Bay Area: a traffic ticket 150, a misdemeanour defence 900, civil 1,400, property 1,100; a public defender if your balance is under 2,000. The verdict is a weighted chance (plan section 3.4) until a real legal system replaces it.

outcomes.name: Plea: the fine as charged, no record
The fine as charged, on the record
The fine and a month's probation

jury.basis: California pays jurors $15 a day (Code Civ. Proc. 215). A summons goes only to someone in the city now (something done in the last online_real_minutes), is open at once and for open_real_hours real hours, and comes at most once in every_real_days REAL days (it had been 30 game days, a day and a half of real time). every_days and notice_days are the old appointment's and are no longer read

business.jail_story_basis: what happens to someone inside in a few days or weeks, told to them as it happened: a fight, the yard, the infirmary, a work detail, the library -- each moving health, stamina and strength the way it would

jail_story.text: Day {d}: a fight broke out in the dayroom and you were caught up in it.
Day {d}: you spent the yard hour on the pull-up bars.
Day {d}: you were in the infirmary with a fever for a day.
Day {d}: kitchen work detail, ten hours on your feet.
Day {d}: a quiet day in the library.
Day {d}: the food was bad and you hardly ate.
Day {d}: no sleep -- the cell block was loud all night.

business.careers_basis: a promotion after 20 shifts with at least 90% of them on time, about 12% more pay a level; late more than 10 minutes and 15 minutes' pay is docked once
business.headhunter_basis: a recruiter looks across the district's openings within 5 km and offers the three that pay best, each at least 10% over what you earn; the fee is 10% of the first month's wage, taken from your pay as it comes

kitchen.basis: the restaurant game (docs/city/kitchen.mjs): a food shop's kitchen, worked by its staff. An ingredient's cost is wholesale, set so a dish's ingredients come to about 28-38% of its menu price (the usual US restaurant food-cost share, approx.). Process seconds are real seconds of play, kept short on purpose; doneness is right within ±15-20% of a process's time, raw well under it and burnt well over it. Tips are a share of the ticket by how well it was made (US restaurant norms of 15-20% for good service, approx.), and a little more for something on the house; the house pays for what it gives away.
kitchen.shake_basis: Spices and salt are measured in shakes: what one shake of a shaker or spice jar puts down (about 0.35 g of fine salt, 0.1 g of ground pepper, 0.12 g of a ground spice, 0.04 g of a dried leafy herb; approx., from the usual 1/4 tsp = 6 shakes of a 1/8-inch shaker hole). potent is how much a gram of it moves the plate's taste (a gram of salt seasons a whole plate), on top of the ordinary per-gram taste.
kitchen.pairs_basis: flavour pairs that lift a dish (tomato-basil, lime-chili...) and clashes that sink it (sweet desserts with fish); a test customer tastes these on top of the dish's balance
kitchen.clashes_basis: each side is an ingredient role (sweet, drink, protein...), or a role with a cuisine (protein:seafood is fish and shellfish)

real_estate.basis: price a square metre of floor by use, at real 2025-26 San Francisco levels (homes about 1,000 a square foot; the housing market's neighbourhood prices refine a home's), scaled by county. The vision's own scale (a plot 40,000) was replaced by real prices at the user's direction; Credits stay at par with the dollar.

tools.basis: a strike's energy: a person's swing of each tool at a typical strength (a framing hammer about 40-60 J, a sledgehammer 300-500 J, a punch 20-40 J; approx., after published impact measurements), scaled by strength from 0.6 at none to 1.4 at full. Against each material the strike counts by how the tool works on it (a saw cuts wood, it does nothing to steel). An object breaks when the energy it has taken reaches its catalogue break_energy_j (docs/object-catalogue.json); a blow far below that counts for less than its share, as a tap does not fell a post.

blunt.name: A blow with what you hold

damage.basis: what breaking a thing costs: the city's public works repair it after a while, and breaking what is not yours is vandalism (California Penal Code 594: a fine, and restitution of the repair). Repair costs approx. 2025 Bay Area contractor prices.

work_tasks.basis: a shift is work: tasks come every minute or so, each done where it is (at the counter, at the kerb, in the back) by walking there and pressing V. Pay is for the time worked, as long as some work was done in each ten minutes; three ten-minute stretches with nothing done and you are sent home. Tips are on top (approx. a few credits a customer).

barista: Serve the customer at the counter
Pull a shot and steam the milk
baker: Pull a tray from the oven
Box a cake for a customer
cook: Take the trash out to the kerb
bartender: Change a keg in the back
Card a customer at the door
parking_attendant: Collect a fee at a car
Direct a car to a space
janitor: Empty the bins at the kerb

errands.basis: a neighbour's errand: buy what they ask at the shops it is sold in and bring it to their door. Paid on the doorstep: what you spent back, and a fee by the distance (approx. a gig-app errand's rate).

transit_lines.basis: buses on the real routes (SFMTA GTFS stops, docs/transit-stops.json): each route's stops in the district, in order along it, joined by the streets; a bus every few minutes each way, stopping at each stop to let people on and off. Headways approx. Muni's frequent network (6-12 minutes). Where Muni's timetable for the district is to hand (docs/city/muni-routes.json, scripts/build_muni_routes.py) its routes run as it runs them instead: one way along their own stops, a bus for each timetabled trip, its number and destination on its sign; headway_min and speed_ms are then the rest's.

npc.basis: residents without a car on a trip too far to walk: the bus where one line serves both ends (most of them: Muni carries far more of San Francisco's car-free trips than cabs do), a taxi for some (approx. one in seven), and for a long way no bus serves; under walk_max_m with no bus, on foot

housing.basis: the homes for sale and to rent, mirroring the market: every residential building's type from its OpenStreetMap tag (house, detached and the like are single-family; apartments and residential are multi-unit, split into units by floor area), a share of each type listed at a time as in San Francisco's market (approx. 2025: about 1% of single-family homes and well under 1% of condos for sale; about 3% of apartments advertised for rent), and prices by square foot and neighbourhood (approx. 2025 medians from public listing-site neighbourhood reports; not a valuation of any real home). The listings turn over each week.

mortgage.basis: a 30-year fixed loan (approx. 6.3%, late 2025), 20% down, closing costs 2% of the price; a payment every 30 days; three missed and the bank forecloses

lease.basis: a month's rent ahead and a month's deposit; rent every 30 days; two missed and the landlord evicts

harm.basis: what a blow or a car does to someone, and a crash to a car. A person on foot hit by a car is hurt by the impact speed (approx., after the pedestrian injury-risk curves of Rosen and Sander 2009 and the AAA Foundation's 2011 study: few serious injuries under 10 mph, most over 25 mph); a blow by its energy (rules.json tools: a punch 20-40 J, a sledgehammer 300-500 J). Each band names the injuries it can be; the kind is recorded with the person, its effects (a limp, a cast) are for a later round. Hospital bills approx. 2025 California emergency charges before insurance. A battery is California Penal Code 242/243(a): a fine of up to $2,000. Cars: the share of condition an impact takes by its speed (a 10 mph bump dents, 25 mph wrecks), towed from where it stopped and repaired at a body shop (approx. 2025 Bay Area rates).

credit.basis: consumer lending as banks do it. The score runs 300-850 on the FICO weights (payment history 35%, amounts owed 30%, length of history 15%, new credit 10%, credit mix 10%; myFICO, 2025), read from the city's own records: bills and loan payments made on time or late, what is owed against free cash and assets, how long you have been here, recent applications, and the kinds of credit handled. Rates follow late-2025 US averages (Federal Reserve G.19: 24-month personal loans about 11-12%; Bankrate: 60-month new-car loans about 7%; SBA 7(a) about 10-12%; medical payment plans 0-9%); online instalment lenders charge about 9 points more and lend to weaker files (state caps: 36% APR). Amounts are whole Credits; a month is 30 game days.

online_store.basis: the city's online store: anything a shop in the city sells, bought from wherever you are and brought to you by courier within the minute, at twice the average in-person price (the convenience premium of app delivery is approx. 1.3-2x after fees and markups; the city's is the top of that). Prescription medicine is not sold online. Services (a doctor's visit, a haircut, a massage) are booked there at their own price, not marked up, and had at the place booked when you get there; the jobs open at the places round you are listed there too, at their pay.

tasks.basis: the task board: work posted round the city, each a few steps with a place to go and a thing to do there, and pay on finishing. Courier pay is the delivery gig's (pickup and drop-off both counted); the Presidio's forestry is the Presidio Trust's removal of dead and hazard trees in its historic forest (a dead, dry 8 cm pole felled in a few dozen axe strokes), paid approx. at day-labour rates; the sightseeing pass is the Marina's own visitors' walk.

forestry.name: Presidio forestry: fell three dead trees

rounds.basis: rounds: a few places to call at, in turn or in any order, paid on the last; at day-labour rates for the walking (a base, so much a stop and so much a km of the round, the km capped at 4). The stops are a few hundred metres apart round where you stand, each reached within reach_m of its door or pole.

flyers.name: Flyers on {street}
flyers.note: five letterboxes on one street, in any order

dog_walk.name: Walk {who}'s dog to {park}
dog_walk.note: fetch the dog, walk it to the park, and bring it home

bus_survey.note: the transit agency's ridership count: stand at each stop

mystery_shopper.name: Mystery shopper: {n} shops
mystery_shopper.note: call at each shop and look round

initiatives.basis: a party's world is governed by the NPC administration until a full council can be elected (vision: mayor and five seats); meanwhile its residents may put measures to a vote of the party, within the platform's limits

toll_carpool_share.label: carpool share of the bridge toll

messages.basis: the words of the city's messages (docs/city/messages.mjs): {braces} are filled in

lawyer.hello_again: Good to hear from you again, {name}. {lawyer} here.
lawyer.hello_close: {name}! It's {lawyer}. Of course I'll take it.
lawyer.taken: I've taken your {charge} case. The hearing is {when}. My honest read: {odds}. I'll keep you posted as it moves.
lawyer.odds_done: It's decided now, but going in I had it at {odds}.
lawyer.evidence_strong: Their evidence is solid, so I'm working the details.
lawyer.evidence_middling: Their evidence has gaps I can work with.
lawyer.evidence_weak: Their evidence is thin. That's good for us.
lawyer.welcome: Any time. That's what I'm here for.
updates_strong: I've asked for the full record from the city. It's detailed, so I'm going through it line by line.
Spoke with the city attorney. They're not in a mood to drop it; I'm preparing to argue the penalty down.
I found a procedural point in the paperwork. It won't win it alone, but it helps.
updates_middling: The record came back. A couple of things don't line up, and I'm going to press on them.
Spoke with the city attorney this morning. There's room to talk, and I told them we'll see them in court.
I've filed our response. Now we wait for the hearing.
updates_weak: The city's evidence is thin. I've filed to have parts of it set aside.
Talked to the city attorney. They know their case is weak; I wouldn't be surprised if it goes our way.
Everything's filed. Honestly, I like where we are.
lawyer.day_before: Reminder: the hearing is {when}, at {court}. Be there in good time. If you don't come, I go in alone and it's harder.
lawyer.hour_before: One hour. I'm on my way to {court}. See you there.
lawyer.absent: You weren't there, so I went in alone.

verdict.dismissed: Good news, {name}: dismissed. The {charge} case is over and you owe nothing on it.
verdict.acquitted: Not guilty, {name}. The {charge} charge is behind you.
verdict.reduced: We got it reduced. You'll owe less on the {charge}; the court sends the new amount.
verdict.record: I'm sorry, {name}. Convicted: it goes on your record. In two years we can look at clearing it.
verdict.probation: Probation. Stay out of trouble while it lasts, and it ends there.
verdict.jail: I'm sorry, {name}. Jail time. I'll be here when you're out.

interview.hello: Hi {name}, I'm {interviewer}. Thanks for applying to be a {title} at {place}. A few quick questions ({n}), then I'll let you know.
interview.thanks: Thanks, that's everything. I'll get back to you within {minutes} minutes.
interview.hired: Good news, {name}: you've got the job. Welcome aboard as our new {title}. Your first shift is {shift}. Clock in when you get here. I'm your boss now, so message me here.
interview.declined: Thanks for your time. We've gone with someone else this time. You're welcome to apply again {when}.

commerce.basis: the object lab's plan (Kerbside-object-lab-2026-11-13, OBJECTS-INTERACTIONS-AND-RESALE-PLAN.md sections 3-6), built in docs/city/things.mjs (one record per thing that needs one), outcomes.mjs (what comes of an act: eligibility, the physical result, what can be recovered, the consequences, drawn once), uses.mjs (what each thing is for) and resale.mjs (selling it again), joined to the world in commerce.mjs. Amounts of money here are whole currency units under keys ending _kcr, turned into minor units by the code (they are not MONEY_KEYS). Probabilities are the lab's tuning proposals for play, not measured rates.

latent.basis: the spread of each material's hidden condition (shares 0-1) a thing's record is made with, seeded by its id: steel rusts, electronics can carry a fault, food and paper get dirty

outcomes.basis: lab plan section 5's starting table: a moderate drop of a sealed meal 75% intact / 20% package damaged / 5% spilled; reclaiming a discarded wooden chair 55% usable wood / 30% damaged / 15% unusable; an authorised wheel removal by p_usable; a crash yields nothing to pick up

found_containers.basis: a box or bag left out (a moving day, a clear-out): its contents drawn once, when it is placed, and the same whoever opens it

uses.basis: what a thing is for, beyond eating it: read it, put it up at home, give it, fit it to your car, mend something with it, cook with it, freshen up with it, fill it, light it, charge with it, lock up with it, post it, sweep up with it, take it apart, test it. Each verb's numbers are the game's; a thing with none here is for carrying, selling or giving.

resale.basis: lab plan section 6: who buys what second-hand, and for what. A buyer's offer is backed by its cash for the day and its stock, quoted for a few hours, never re-rolled by asking again. Prepared food, opened groceries, medicine and used safety gear are not resold; stolen, borrowed, impounded, reserved and delivery goods are blocked until their custody is sorted.

blocked_food.note: prepared food and medicine are not resold: eat it, return it, or throw it away

safety.note: opened hygiene goods, medicine and used safety gear are not resold

sealed_groceries.note: only sealed, in-date groceries, and only a few

services.note: a service is had, not owned

specialist.name: Specialist buy-back
specialist.note: knows what it is worth, and tests it

consignment.name: Consignment
consignment.note: the shop sells it for you, slower, for a share

listing.name: Bulletin board

shipped.name: Shipped listing
shipped.tax_policy: sales tax on the item only; the carrier's charge passed through untaxed (game policy v1)
shipped.note: reaches further; 8% commission, the buyer pays the carrier and the tax
